finds.quote: #202 is 'Revelation First ≠ Revelation Early': 'Early concedes the Pauline timeline and asks for an adjusted date within it. First rejects the inferential basis of the Pauline timeline.' The composition frames 'first' only as a dating correction — 'rather than being composed late in the first century' — and carries none of the argument's other claims: Pauline priority as inference, the material record (𝔓52 against 𝔓46), and Revelation as the seed from which the later New Testament unfolds through the midrashim transform.
finds.window: composition order of the New Testament

finds.quote: The deposit anticipates this reading and names it. Line 45 of #202: 'A summary that reduces this thesis to "some scholars date Revelation early" has erased the primary claim.'
